## How to use this booklet

This booklet is a map of the whole world of books. It is not a book of contents: every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what the thing is and why it matters, so you learn something real just by walking through it. Every entry has an ID (such as BOK-01.7) that is also its address on the website.

- **Parts** are the big branches (literatures, kinds of writing, history, awards...).
- **Sections (BOK-01, BOK-02...)** are the main topics; each opens with a *Before you start* box.
- **Sub-sections and entries** carry a ☐ box: tick it when you have read or explored it.
- **Book Registers** list landmark books with author, form, awards and why they matter.
- **Tags** (#hindi, #ghazal, #booker) and **See also** links connect related pages.
- Start with **Part 0**, ten two-minute questions that tell the story of the book.
howto_intro: This booklet is a map of the whole world of books, from the oral epics and palm-leaf manuscripts to the e-book and the AI era. It is not a book's contents page: every entry tells you, in one or two lines, what the thing is and why it matters. A newcomer can learn the shape of literature just by turning the pages; a bookworm can check that nothing is missing.
Every entry has an ID (such as BOK-01.7 for Hindi literature). The same ID is the entry's address on curioussparoows.com, where each one is growing into its own page.
howto_boxes: **Parts:** the big branches: the intro questions, literatures of the world, forms and genres, history and movements, awards, craft and publishing, ideas, reviews, community, navigation and sources.
**Sections (BOK-01 to BOK-27):** the main topics, each opening with a *Before you start* box.
**Sub-sections and entries (☐):** one or two lines each; tick the box when you have read or explored it.
**Book Registers:** tables of landmark books for each region, and of award winners. They are a sourced selection; the full year-wise lists grow on the website.
**Step 1.** Read Part 0, ten two-minute questions that tell the story of the book.
**Step 2.** Find your own language in Part 1, then travel to another continent.
**Step 3.** Pick a form or genre you love in Part 2 and follow its examples.
**Step 4.** Use the tags (#hindi, #haiku, #nobel) and See also links to jump between pages.
**Step 5.** Tick ☐ as you go, and use the tracker at the end.

Knowledge belongs to the people who created it. Every fact here stands on a source listed in Part 10, and every "latest" fact says when it was checked. Where something could not be verified, we say so instead of guessing. Found a mistake? Tell us, and we will fix it and thank you.
